newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end down, short-term rates up.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end down, short-term rates up.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds ended slighlty down on Wednesday on advanced bond buying in the belief the yields would fall further, dealers said.
But average overnight call rates and CDs yields rose as banks were tight on liquidity on the eve of twice-a-monthly deadline for the central bank won reserve requirement.
* 3-yr corporates closed down at 12.19 vs 12.20 pct
* 3-mth CDs closed up at 12.65 vs 12.60 pct
* Overnight average call rate at 12.49 vs 12.27 pct
New corporate bond issues in June were projected to be 2.9 trillion won, up 18.4 percent from May. Some dealers feared supply would exceed demand.
The overnight call rate rose as banks were tight on liquidity on the eve of the central bank won reserve requirement, dealers said.
They said three-month CD yields and commerical paper (CP) rates rose in line with call rates. CP rates ended up 0.05 percentage points at 12.65, they said.
